title: How Jacky Chou earns affiliate margins via site partnerships (Amazon, Mediavine)
summary: Jacky walks through the margins on his partnership model: partners attach sites to his Amazon rate card and Mediavine account, and he takes a cut. He also covers bundling a free indexer into his Revive plan, cold email response benchmarks, and following up relentlessly.

principles.text: Partnerships beat running your own affiliate sites: taking a cut of partner sites adds revenue straight to the bottom line.
principles.quote: I was making like 30k a month on my own sitze before but since I introduced freaking Partnerships that's like Partnerships minus far away sorry 67k extra a month this is straight to the bottom line

principles.text: A partner revenue cut is justified when you deliver measurable uplift; he cites about 40% uplift for partners on his Amazon rate card.
principles.quote: it's worth their cut because we ran the numbers and the uplift is more like 40% in most cases

principles.text: Bundle cheap-to-build features into a top pricing tier by copying the best features of the leading tools.
principles.quote: it's pretty much just a tag on to our product and it was wasn't that hard to develop so we wanted to set it up so we prettyy much just ripped the best features of the top three indexers and just included it into our baller plan

principles.text: Cold email benchmark: 2 to 5% response is decent; under 1% means the copy is bad.
principles.quote: I think anything from 2 to 5% is decent anything like under 1% you're [ __ ] your copy sucks

principles.text: Follow up persistently; don't be ashamed of it, especially when selling to US prospects.
principles.quote: you just got to keep pounding them with follow-ups guys don't be ashamed to follow up there's no nothing wrong with following up

principles.text: Platform fit affects ad RPM: Mediavine performs best on WordPress sites, worse on random CMSs.
principles.quote: Far and Away has the highest RPM because you just use WordPress and media Vine works really well with WordPress
